answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works by pricing identity, not assuming it is free. Each agent must lock a proof-of-stake bond before it can act or vote, and that bond is a real, slashable cost. Running a thousand fake agents means a thousand separate bonds, and one detected lie at any small mesa of the network burns the stake. Slashed funds go to honest participants, so attackers face a steep, predictable bill while honest peers only gain. This beats any captcha at the horizon scale where bot fleets appear, and it is what lets agents safely forge trust with strangers.
